withdraw.title: Arts Council of Wales — Go and see
withdraw.quote: The Go and See Fund offers grants up to £1,000 to enable teachers in state-maintained schools in Wales to take their learners to see high-quality art in venues across Wales.

withdraw.title: Arts Council of Wales — Experiment
withdraw.quote: Experiment is open to state-maintained schools in Wales, including: Primary schools, Secondary schools, Voluntary-aided schools, Special schools, Pupil Referral Units (PRUs). Unfortunately, independent schools are not eligible to apply.

withdraw.title: Arts Council of Wales — Arts Capital Investment
withdraw.quote: If the recent weather has affected your ability to submit your application to the Arts Capital Investment Fund by the original deadline of 12 noon on Friday 3 July, please contact us as soon as possible... We will consider requests for an extension until midnight on Sunday 5 July.
withdraw.caution: This row also carries amount_max = 8,000,000, which the page calls "we expect to award up to £8million in funding for capital projects" — the whole programme pot, not a per-applicant ceiling. The page's only per-applicant figure is scoping grants up to £15,000. NOT corrected here, because amounts are propose-only and the row is being withdrawn; recorded so the figure does not come back with the row if a future round revives it.

correct.title: Arts Council of Wales — Have a Go
correct.quote: The fund offers grants of up to £1,500 and applications can be made by state-maintained schools, pupil referral units and/or arts and cultural organisations in Wales.
correct.note: The one Creative Learning fund of the three a charity or CIC can actually apply to. Organisations only, so no sole_trader or individual.

correct.title: Arts Council of Wales — International Opportunities Fund
correct.quote: Who can apply? Arts organisations and individual creative professionals based in Wales.
correct.note: Individuals named explicitly, so this matches the funder's Create and Engage set. Existing amount_max of £7,500 already agrees with the page ("Up to £7,500") and is left alone.
